"Mayne, Moran, do your country proud, eh?" 

Having reached an amiable agreement, Almstedt would depart from the facility together with his personal entourage, departing back in the Springflame aircraft. Ulf Mayne and Freya Moran, as SummitONE's designated representatives in Sal-Baliz, would be left behind along with a respectable platoon of around 50 SummitONE contractors, all formally falling under Mandhir's direct command.

[b]SummitONE Seagates | [sub]Austmark Island and Cape Zurekdal | 17 March 2025[/sub][/b]

Following peak revenues at the tail end of 2024, the Board of Directors of the Almstedt Corporation and SummitONE Solutions have joinly decided to establish a new project division within SummitONE's corporate administration: SummitONE Seagates, a maritime infrastructural development and planning authority dedicated towards construction and maintenance of its eponym: The Seagates, a novel strategic military-civilian port design that could be jointly used for rapid deployment and trade management.

Austmark Island would be the site of the first Seagate, officially named Seagate One (stylized as Seagate Austmark), which will act as the major maritime and aerial link between Austmark and Mainland High Albany. Xavier Almstedt would be temporarily designated as Chairman of Seagate Austmark's corporate administration pending new hires. At its peak, Seagate One is expected to generate anywhere from 10,000 to 15,000 jobs over the course of half a month, with more to come as more Seagate projects begin to go under construction elsewhere across Erene.

Covertly, operating beyond congressional oversight, SummitONE Solutions would also receive a special grant courtesy of the White Sea Caucus to establish Seagate Zurekdal in Cape Zurekdal, known locally as the  [i]Wadi Zurayq[/i] (lit. "Little Blue Valley"), a large geographic protrusion in Northern West Shamat overlooking Orman to the south and Inostrancevia to the north. While officially slated to be a commercial enterprise to expand High Albany's global reach beyond the Baliwick Sea, Seagate Zurekdal would in actuality be envisioned as a transit route to aid in SummitONE's covert support for Sal-Baliz. SummitONE executives Ulf Mayne and Freya Moran would be appointed to oversee construction in West Shamat.

While Seagate Zurekdal was pending finalization, a fleet of dark ships would begin shipping construction materials and machinery to Sal-Baliz through the Baliwick Sea to begin the first phase of Xavier Almstedt's agreement with the supreme leader.

Construction for both Seagates is expected to begin immediately, with Seagate Austmark likely to cost over 50 billion CD$ over the course of four years. Seagate Zurekdal, with its much smaller scope and price at around only 12 billion CD$, is expected to be accomplished within the year and be partially operational within four months, with SummitONE aiming to implement a novel new modular port design dubbed the "Rapid Deployment Module" or RDM for short, which will form the structural core of the Seagates.

Described on SummitONE's official website as [i]"... a high-efficiency, prefabricated system of systems"[/i], the RDM will consist of factory-built components like barracks, docks, and storage units; caisson-based floating platforms for civilian and small-scale docks; scalable power sources like floating solar farms and nuclear microreactors courtesy of the Ministry of Energy; desalination barges; and fully AI-run terminals to drastically increase labor efficiency. Upon the installation of these RDMs, more permanant infrastructural systems are expected to be constructed to transform these prefabricated docks into fully idealized Seagates for international use.

Along with other identified sponsors, the Seagates program will be expected to operate in partnership with the Almstedt Corporation and Dearborn Bank, both of whom will serve as the primary investors for the first two Seagates.
